docs.title: The Tactic
docs.text:
A tactic is a typed unit of work. It declares what it accepts and what it returns, validates both on every call, and describes itself in a form that services, packages, and other agents can read. That one boundary is what lets the same piece of work be:

  • validated: input and output are checked against Pydantic types;
  • streamed: chunks and events have one shape for every runtime;
  • served: any tactic becomes a FastAPI app with /run, /stream, /info;
  • packaged: an lllm.toml entry points at it by name and ref;
  • composed: other tactics, Pydantic AI agents, and channel processors call it without knowing how it is implemented.

There is one class to learn:

from lllm import Tactic

lllm.Tactic is the native program class, with agents, per-call sessions, and batch calls. It subclasses lllm.protocol.Tactic, the runtime-neutral base that supplies the typed boundary: run(), arun(), stream(), aevents(), and info(). Adapters for other runtimes (plain functions, Pydantic AI, remote services) are protocol tactics too, so everything on this page applies to them.

docs.title: Two ways to write one
docs.text:
Write the program in call(), or implement the protocol hook _run(). Both produce a tactic that validates, serves, and packages the same way.

Program: call()Hook: _run() 
from pydantic import BaseModel
from lllm import Tactic


class Question(BaseModel):
    text: str


class Answer(BaseModel):
    text: str


class Shout(Tactic):
    """Shout the question back."""

    name = "shout"
    input_type = Question
    output_type = Answer

    def call(self, task: Question) -> Answer:
        return Answer(text=task.text.upper())


shout = Shout()
print(shout.run({"text": "hello"}))   # text='HELLO'
print(shout({"text": "hello"}))       # text='HELLO'
print(shout.info().runtime_kind)      # native

from pydantic import BaseModel
from lllm import Tactic


class Question(BaseModel):
    text: str


class Answer(BaseModel):
    text: str


class ShoutHook(Tactic[Question, Answer]):
    """Shout the question back."""

    name = "shout"
    input_type = Question
    output_type = Answer

    def _run(self, input_value: Question, *, context=None) -> Answer:
        return Answer(text=input_value.text.upper())


shout = ShoutHook()
print(shout.run({"text": "hello"}))   # text='HELLO'
print(shout.info().runtime_kind)      # python

The input arrives as a dict here and reaches your code as a Question. The return value is checked against Answer before the caller sees it.

call() program _run() hook run(), arun(), info(), serving, packaging, use as a tool yes yes tactic(task), acall, bcall, ccall yes yes Runs inside a TacticCallSession every call calls through tactic(task), acall, bcall, ccall Runs on a per-call copy with fresh agent_group agents every call never: hooks run on the instance info().runtime_kind "native" "python" ("native" with an agent_group) Receives the validated task, and context= when call accepts it the validated input and a CallContext

tactic(task) and the other native entry points run call() when the class writes one, else its _run() hook (or _arun()). A hook-only tactic has no call(): tactic.call(task) raises TacticUnsupportedError and points you to the entry points, and a hook that hands its call back with super()._run() or self.call() raises the same error instead of recursing. A tactic that writes only _arun() still gets run(), which runs arun() to completion, and an async def call() is awaited on every entry point.

docs.title: Typed input and output
docs.text:
input_type and output_type accept anything Pydantic can validate: BaseModel subclasses, builtins such as str or int, list[str], Literal[...], dataclasses, and TypedDicts. input_model and output_model are aliases, so tactics written with the native names publish their schemas too. A class's own input_model wins over an input_type it inherits.

from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from lllm import SchemaError, Tactic


class Review(BaseModel):
    text: str = Field(min_length=1)
    stars: int = Field(ge=1, le=5)


class Verdict(BaseModel):
    label: Literal["positive", "negative"]
    confidence: float


class Classify(Tactic):
    """Label a product review."""

    name = "classify"
    input_type = Review
    output_type = Verdict

    def call(self, task: Review) -> Verdict:
        positive = task.stars >= 4
        # A plain dict is fine: the output is validated into Verdict.
        return {"label": "positive" if positive else "negative", "confidence": 0.9}


classify = Classify()
print(repr(classify.run({"text": "Works great", "stars": 5})))
print(repr(classify.run(Review(text="Broke in a day", stars=1))))

try:
    classify.run({"text": "", "stars": 9})
except SchemaError as exc:
    print(str(exc).splitlines()[0])

Verdict(label='positive', confidence=0.9)
Verdict(label='negative', confidence=0.9)
Value does not match schema Review: 2 validation errors for Review

A few rules worth knowing:

  • Input can be a model instance or JSON-compatible data. Output can be the model or data that validates into it.
  • A failed check on either side raises SchemaError.
  • The generic parameters in Tactic[Review, Verdict] are for type checkers only. Validation and the published JSON schemas come from input_type and output_type; a tactic without them passes values through unchecked.
  • Pydantic's normal coercion applies, so input_type = int accepts "21".

docs.title: Calling a tactic
docs.text:
Every tactic has the protocol methods:

Method Returns run(value, *, context=None, return_trace=False, **kwargs) The validated output, or a CallResult when return_trace=True. await arun(value, *, context=None, return_trace=False, **kwargs) The same, async. stream(value, *, context=None, **kwargs) An iterator of chunks, for tactics that stream. astream(...) An async iterator of chunks. aevents(...) An async iterator of TacticEvents. info() The TacticInfo contract. supports(name), capabilities() Whether a capability such as "stream" is available.

Extra keyword arguments to run() and arun() are passed through to call() or _run().

lllm.Tactic adds the native entry points, for both styles:

Method Returns tactic(task, session_name=None, tags=None, metadata=None, return_session=False, **kwargs) The result, or the call's TacticCallSession. await tactic.acall(task, ...) The same, awaited: an async def call() runs on the caller's loop, a sync one in a worker thread. tactic.bcall(tasks, max_workers=None, fail_fast=True, return_sessions=False, ...) Results in input order. With fail_fast=False, failures come back as exception objects in place. async for index, result in tactic.ccall(tasks) (index, result) pairs as each call finishes.

tactic(task) validates input and output the same way run() does.

docs.title: Traces
docs.text:
return_trace=True returns a CallResult with the output and a CallTrace (request id, state, latency, type names, and the error if there was one). Failures are recorded instead of raised:

from lllm import CallContext

result = shout.run(
    {"text": "hi"},
    context=CallContext(request_id="req-1", metadata={"user": "ada"}),
    return_trace=True,
)
print(result.output)
print(result.trace.state, result.trace.request_id, result.trace.metadata)

failed = shout.run({"text": 5}, return_trace=True)
print(failed.output, failed.trace.state, failed.trace.error_type)

text='HI'
success req-1 {'user': 'ada'}
None failure SchemaError

docs.title: Streaming and events
docs.text:
Implement stream() to make a tactic stream. Yield whatever chunks make sense, and yield a TacticEvent when you want to label one:

from lllm import Tactic, TacticEvent


class Countdown(Tactic):
    """Count down, then lift off."""

    name = "countdown"
    input_type = int
    output_type = str

    def call(self, task: int) -> str:
        return "liftoff"

    def stream(self, task: int, *, context=None):
        for n in range(task, 0, -1):
            yield n
        yield TacticEvent.result("liftoff")


countdown = Countdown()
print(countdown.info().capabilities)
print(list(countdown.stream(3))[:3])

('acall', 'arun', 'call', 'run', 'stream')
[3, 2, 1]

astream() validates the input the same way run() does and then iterates stream() on a worker thread, one item per request, so stream() receives the typed value, a slow stream never blocks the event loop, and nothing runs ahead of the reader. Closing the async iterator closes the generator on that thread: when it is waiting at a yield, its cleanup has run by the time aclose() returns; otherwise it runs once the item in progress is done. aevents() wraps every chunk from astream() that is not already an event as TacticEvent(kind="message", data=chunk). aevents() is what the service's /stream route sends:

import asyncio


async def show():
    async for event in countdown.aevents(2):
        print(event.kind, event.data)


asyncio.run(show())

message 2
message 1
result liftoff

A TacticEvent has id, timestamp, kind, data, and metadata. TacticEvent.result(value) and TacticEvent.error(message) build the two common kinds. Override astream() when the source is natively async, or aevents() to control the event stream yourself; the tactic then advertises "stream" or "events" in its capabilities. On lllm.Tactic, a synchronous events() generator works too: aevents() and /stream serve it, passing it the validated input and wrapping plain items as message events. There, each stream runs like call(), on a per-call copy with fresh agents and its own session.

Calling stream() directly skips that validation and passes the argument through as given, so pass it a typed value (or call self.validate_input(value) yourself). A tactic that does not stream raises TacticUnsupportedError from stream().

docs.title: CallContext
docs.text:
CallContext is the request metadata that travels with one call: ids for correlating logs and traces, who called, and free-form tags and metadata.

from lllm import CallContext

context = CallContext(
    trace_id="trace-42",
    caller="nightly-job",
    tags={"team": "research"},
    metadata={"user": "ada"},
)
Field Meaning request_id Unique id for this call. Generated (a UUID) when omitted. caller Who is calling: a service, worker, or user label. trace_id, span_id Distributed-tracing ids. tags String-to-string labels. metadata Any JSON-compatible values. package_ref, service_ref, tactic_ref, endpoint Where the call is going; services fill in tactic_ref and endpoint.

Id fields must be plain tokens (no whitespace or path separators); the model rejects anything else.

How the context reaches your code:

  • _run(input_value, *, context) always gets a CallContext, through every entry point; one is created when the caller passes none.
  • call() gets context= when its signature declares context (or **kwargs). Under run() it is a CallContext; under tactic(task) it is None unless the caller passes context=.
  • Pass a CallContext. Anything else, such as a dict, raises TypeError from run() and arun(), and from tactic(task), acall, bcall, and ccall when the program is a _run() or _arun() hook. Those four pass a call() program the value unchecked: a dict arrives as a dict.
class WhoAsked(Tactic):
    name = "who-asked"
    output_type = dict

    def call(self, task: str, *, context=None) -> dict:
        return {"task": task, "caller": context.caller if context else None}


print(WhoAsked().run("summarize", context=context))
print(WhoAsked()("summarize"))

{'task': 'summarize', 'caller': 'nightly-job'}
{'task': 'summarize', 'caller': None}

Services build the context from the request's context object, and RemoteTactic sends it, so a trace_id set by a caller arrives in the call() of a tactic running in another process. Keep configuration (models, keys, runtime settings) on the tactic or its runtime; the context is per request.

docs.title: Describing a tactic: info()
docs.text:
info() returns the tactic's public contract as a TacticInfo. Services return it from /info, lllm inspect prints it, and the hub renders it into package cards.

shout = Shout(
    package_ref="lllm://demo/shout/tactics/shout",
    examples=[{"input": {"text": "hi"}, "output": {"text": "HI"}}],
    metadata={"owner": "docs"},
)
print(shout.info().model_dump_json(indent=2))

{
  "name": "shout",
  "description": "Shout the question back.",
  "input_schema": {
    "properties": {
      "text": {
        "title": "Text",
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    "required": [
      "text"
    ],
    "title": "Question",
    "type": "object"
  },
  "output_schema": {
    "properties": {
      "text": {
        "title": "Text",
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    "required": [
      "text"
    ],
    "title": "Answer",
    "type": "object"
  },
  "capabilities": [
    "acall",
    "arun",
    "call",
    "run"
  ],
  "runtime_kind": "native",
  "package_ref": "lllm://demo/shout/tactics/shout",
  "service_ref": null,
  "examples": [
    {
      "input": {
        "text": "hi"
      },
      "output": {
        "text": "HI"
      }
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "owner": "docs"
  }
}
Field Source name name= passed to the constructor, else the class attribute name, else the class name. An Enum member gives its value. It must be one path segment: no /, \, :, ;, or %. description description=, else the class attribute, else your class's docstring. input_schema, output_schema JSON Schema exported from input_type and output_type. capabilities run, arun, plus call/acall on lllm.Tactic, and stream/events when implemented. runtime_kind native, python, pydantic-ai, http, proxy, or sandbox for the built-in tactics. A class that sets runtime_kind passes it on to its subclasses. package_ref, service_ref An lllm://.../tactics/... ref and a service ref or URL; see Refs. examples, metadata Whatever you pass to the constructor.

The constructor keywords name, description, package_ref, service_ref, examples, and metadata work on your own tactics. The built-in wrappers take fewer: RemoteTactic takes name and metadata and fills in service_ref and metadata["url"] from its URL, ProxyTactic takes name, description, and metadata, and SandboxedTactic takes name and description. /info and lllm inspect drop secret-shaped metadata keys such as api_key, token, password, and cookie while keeping references such as api_key_ref. Even so, keep secrets out of metadata.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Exception Raised when SchemaError Input or output fails validation, or a type cannot be exported as JSON Schema. TacticUnsupportedError The tactic lacks the requested capability: no call() or _run(), call() on a tactic that implements _run() instead, or stream() on a tactic that does not stream. TacticRefError An lllm:// tactic ref is malformed or not bound. RemoteTacticError A remote service answered with an error; see Services. TypeError context is not a CallContext where one is required (see CallContext), or return_trace is not a bool. 
LLLMError (RuntimeError)
└── ProtocolError
    ├── SchemaError
    └── TacticError
        ├── TacticUnsupportedError
        ├── TacticLoadError
        ├── TacticRefError
        └── TacticServiceError
            └── RemoteTacticError

All of these import from lllm. Exceptions raised by your own code propagate unchanged. When a tactic running in a session fails, the lllm.runtimes.native.core.tactic logger writes one INFO line with the error (the traceback goes to DEBUG), the session's state becomes "failure", and its error_traceback keeps the traceback. Over HTTP, SchemaError and TacticUnsupportedError become 400 responses and other exceptions become 500s, both with a structured body (Services).

docs.title: Sessions for call() programs
docs.text:
Each call of a call() program runs on a fresh copy of the tactic inside a TacticCallSession. Ask for it with return_session=True:

class Upper(Tactic):
    name = "upper"

    def call(self, task: str) -> str:
        return task.upper()


class Twice(Tactic):
    name = "twice"

    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.upper = Upper()  # a tactic attribute becomes a sub-tactic

    def call(self, task: str) -> str:
        return self.upper(task) + " " + self.upper(task)


twice = Twice()
session = twice("hi", return_session=True)
print(session.state, repr(session.delivery))
print(session.sub_tactic_call_count, list(session.sub_tactic_sessions))
print(twice.bcall(["a", "b"]))

success 'HI HI'
2 ['upper']
['A A', 'B B']

A session records state, delivery (the result), error and error_traceback on failure, every agent call in agent_sessions, and every sub-tactic session in sub_tactic_sessions. total_cost, agent_call_count, and sub_tactic_call_count roll everything up, and summary() returns a small dict for logs. When a tactic that runs in a session is called while another program is running, its session is recorded in the caller's under the tactic's name (the constructor's name= when given). That includes calls made from bcall worker threads and through a Resolver. call() programs always run in a session. A _run() hook gets one only through tactic(task), acall, bcall, and ccall, not under run() or arun(). Tactics that are not lllm.Tactic subclasses (wrapped functions, Pydantic AI and remote tactics) do not create sessions.

docs.title: Agents
docs.text:
Set agent_group and pass agent configs, and every call gets fresh native agents in self.agents, each tracked by the call's session. Agents reach models through LiteLLM by default (pip install "lllm-core[native]"). This example calls a model, so it needs a provider key (for example OPENAI_API_KEY):

from lllm import Tactic


class Brief(Tactic):
    name = "brief"
    agent_group = ["writer", "critic"]

    def call(self, task: str) -> str:
        writer, critic = self.agents["writer"], self.agents["critic"]
        writer.open("draft")
        writer.receive(task)
        draft = writer.respond().content
        critic.open("review")
        critic.receive(draft)
        return critic.respond().content


config = {
    "global": {"model_name": "gpt-4o-mini"},
    "agent_configs": [
        {"name": "writer", "system_prompt": "You write a three-bullet brief."},
        {"name": "critic", "system_prompt": "You tighten the brief. Reply with the final text."},
    ],
}

brief = Brief(config)
session = brief("Why typed tactic boundaries matter", return_session=True)
print(session.delivery)
print(session.agent_call_count, session.total_cost)

For a single agent with no configuration at all, Tactic.quick() returns the reply (or, without a query, the agent itself):

from lllm import Tactic

reply = Tactic.quick("In one sentence, what is a tactic?", model="gpt-4o-mini")
print(reply.content)

Agents, prompts, configs, and the call loop are covered in the Tactic reference and the Agent reference.

docs.title: Which style to use
docs.text:
• call() for agentic programs: the tactic orchestrates native agents or other tactics, and you want a session with cost roll-up on every call.
  • _run() for deterministic steps, adapters, and glue code that only needs the typed boundary. For a single function, as_tactic(fn) is shorter still (Runtimes).
  • Wrap, don't subclass, when the work already lives elsewhere: PydanticAITactic for Pydantic AI agents and RemoteTactic for running services (Runtimes).

Callers cannot tell the difference: they use run(), arun(), and stream(), and services and packages read the same info().

docs.title: Design lineage
docs.text:
The tactic boundary grew out of the reusable reasoning units in Analytica, which decomposes complex societal, economic, political, and scientific questions into grounded subpropositions, runs specialized agents or tools over them, and synthesizes the results into a more stable analysis. LLLM keeps the boundary and drops the domain: a tactic is not tied to propositional reasoning, forecasting, or any one agent architecture.

Apeiron applied the same boundary to autonomous software development: full-lifecycle application synthesis with demand modeling, computer-use agent evaluation, activity tracing, and locality-controlled iteration. Analysis agents, software-building agents, evaluators, tools, and deployment services all fit behind one small, typed callable.

  • Cheng, Junyan, Kyle Richardson, and Peter Chin. "Analytica: Soft Propositional Reasoning for Robust and Scalable LLM-Driven Analysis." The Fourteenth International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR), 2026.
  • Cheng, Junyan, Ankit Srivastava, Jessie Zeng, Milenko Drinic, and Jack W. Stokes. "Apeiron: A Scalable LLM-agentic Framework for Autonomous Full-lifecycle Demand-optimized Application Synthesis." Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2026, 2026, pp. 3868-3899.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
lllm is the single command. Module command groups (hub, network, shell) take their own options before the subcommand.

lllm create   NAME [--template T]   new project
lllm init     [PATH]                write lllm.toml
lllm setup    [TARGET]              store the API keys a package declares
lllm inspect  TARGET                tactic metadata, or what serve would launch
lllm serve    TARGET                serve a tactic or a package resource
lllm hub      ...                   validate, publish, read, index packages
lllm network  ...                   SSSN channel stores (experimental)
lllm shell    ...                   AAAX strategies (experimental)

TARGET is a module:attribute entrypoint (imported from the current directory) or a package path (a folder with lllm.toml, or the file itself).

docs.title: lllm create
docs.text:
lllm create my-app                         # native project, template "minimal"
lllm create my-app --template pipeline     # pipeline | proxy | research | service
lllm create my-app --template ./my-template  # a folder with lllm-template.toml
lllm create plain my-svc                   # service scaffolds: plain | pydantic-ai | native
Option Default --template minimal Template name or folder --model gpt-4o-mini Model written into configs/default.yaml --directory . Parent folder --force off Overwrite existing files

Native templates create lllm.toml, prompts/, configs/default.yaml, tactics/, main.py (with create_tactic()), and an offline smoke test.

docs.title: lllm init
docs.text:
lllm init [PATH] [--name NAME] [--org ORG] [--kind KIND] [--force]

Writes a minimal lllm.toml (with [card] and [docs.readme]) and a README if there is none. See The manifest.

docs.title: lllm setup
docs.text:
lllm setup ./briefs                       # prompts for missing keys
lllm setup ./briefs --credentials env --env-file .env.local --set OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
lllm setup --show-conventions             # common provider key names

Reads [requirements.api_keys], plus the required_api_keys metadata of the resource lllm serve would launch (or the one named with --resource), and stores missing keys in the OS keyring (secure extra) or a local env file. A package with nothing to launch, such as a library, is set up from its [requirements.api_keys] alone. --credentials auto uses the keyring when available.

docs.title: lllm inspect
docs.text:
lllm inspect tactics:Shout --json     # name, schemas, capabilities, endpoints
lllm inspect ./briefs                 # resolved resource, port, routes, key status

Package options: --resource section.name, --store DIR (channel resources), --env-file, --no-keyring.

docs.title: lllm serve
docs.text:
lllm serve tactics:Shout --port 8000
lllm serve ./briefs                       # the package's primary resource
lllm serve ./briefs --resource services.api
Option Default --host 127.0.0.1 Bind address (host or IP, not a URL) --port declared port or 8000 --log-level info Uvicorn log level --resource [package] primary Resource to launch --store <package>/.lllm/network Store root for channel resources --credentials, --env-file, --no-keyring Key lookup and interactive setup --skip-key-check off Start without checking declared keys

An entrypoint names a tactic class or instance, a factory, an object with a run method, or a handler function (Loading entrypoints). A resource that cannot be launched, or a service entry that fails to import or build, stops with an error that names the cause (Services).

docs.title: lllm hub
docs.text:
lllm hub [--hub DIR] COMMAND

--hub defaults to .lllm/hub.

Command init [PATH] Same as lllm init validate PATH Validate a package publish PATH --local [--no-validate] Publish into the local hub list Published packages (org/name@version) get ID [--dest DIR] [--version V] Download a package card ID, agent-card ID Render the package card / agent card config-template ID Render a starting .lllm/config.toml index OUTPUT [--generated-at TS] Write a static catalog for the hub web app serve [--host] [--port 8787] Serve the hub API

See The Hub.

docs.title: lllm network
docs.text:
lllm network [--store DIR] COMMAND

--store defaults to .lllm/network. Commands: channels, create-channel, get-channel, append, query-events, get-event, create-subscription, get-subscription, pull-subscription, write-artifact, get-artifact, read-artifact, put-snapshot, get-snapshot, serve. See SSSN.

docs.title: lllm shell
docs.text:
lllm shell inspect TARGET [--json]
lllm shell serve TARGET [--host] [--port 8400] [--log-level]

TARGET is a strategy.py file, a folder (with strategy.py, shell.py, or lllm.toml), or a module:factory. See AAAX.

docs.title: Hub Metadata
docs.text:
Helpers that export what a tactic or channel publishes, in the shape the hub indexes. Use them to fill metadata in lllm.toml or to build catalog entries.

from lllm.hub import tactic_resource
from lllm.network import Channel, channel_resource, snapshot_resource

resource = tactic_resource(EchoTactic())
channel = channel_resource(Channel(name="events", form="log", description="Raw events."))

tactic_resource(tactic) returns:

Key Content name, description, runtime From tactic.info() capabilities run, arun, stream, call, ... endpoints Custom @endpoint routes: name, method, path, mode, description, tags input_schema, output_schema JSON schemas of the typed input and output package_ref, service_ref lllm:// refs or a service URL examples, metadata Public examples and metadata

channel_resource and snapshot_resource do the same for SSSN channels and snapshots, including custom store endpoints.

docs.title: Rules for published metadata
docs.text:
Package refs use lllm://org/package/tactics/name. Service refs use either lllm://org/package/services/name or an absolute HTTP(S) URL without embedded credentials, params, queries, fragments, percent escapes, backslashes, colons, empty segments, or dot segments.

tactic_resource drops secret-shaped keys from examples and metadata: API keys, tokens, passwords, secrets, cookies, authorization, credentials, and private keys, in snake_case, kebab-case, camelCase, and collapsed forms (api_key, x-api-key, apiKey, apikey, accessToken, clientSecret, set-cookie, sessionCookie, proxyAuthorization, awsCredentials, privateKey, ...). A token key is token or ends in token (accessToken, eos_token), so token_limit is kept. References to secrets are kept: api_key_ref, apiKeyRef, apikeyref. channel_resource and snapshot_resource copy metadata unchanged. Metadata maps must use string keys, including nested maps.

In lllm.toml these keys are errors, not dropped: the package ships the file as written, so lllm hub validate reports metadata_secret_key for them in the metadata and extra keys of named resource tables, [config], and [card] (see Validation). Validation does not look inside maps under JSON-schema keys (schema, input_schema, output_schema, or forms such as inputSchema), where a field may be named api_key, or inside [config] defaults and tactic examples.

Cards, the hub API, and the static catalog drop these keys from resource metadata, including [config] defaults and tactic examples. They also drop any key with a token word part, such as token_limit, which validation allows. Inside schema maps, cards and the catalog still drop secret-shaped keys, but the hub API returns those maps unchanged. The package zip contains lllm.toml as written, so every key validation allows ships in it.

docs.title: Service API
docs.text:
The FastAPI adapter exposes a tactic through portable endpoints.

Endpoint Use GET /health {"ok": true, "tactics": [...]}. GET /info Return service-advertised TacticInfo. POST /run Run the tactic with envelope or raw JSON input. POST /stream Stream tactic output when supported. GET /tactics, GET /tactics/{name}/info TacticInfo for every tactic, or for one. POST /tactics/{name}/run, POST /tactics/{name}/stream Run or stream one tactic.

create_tactic_app mounts all of them. create_service_app mounts /health and the /tactics/... routes, and /info, /run, and /stream too when it holds one tactic and expose_single_tactic_routes=True. /openapi.json documents the tactic's input schema in the /run and /stream request envelopes and its output schema in the /run response.

Custom endpoints declared with @endpoint.* are mounted alongside these portable routes. They must use unique method/path pairs and must not shadow reserved LLLM service routes such as /run, /stream, /info, or /tactics/{name}/run. Endpoint paths, names, and tags must avoid whitespace and percent escapes; paths must also avoid // network-path prefixes, empty or dot segments, backslashes, colons, semicolon path params, query strings, and fragments. A GET or DELETE endpoint called without a body receives the query parameters as a dict (or None) instead of a validated input.

Public info endpoints filter raw secret-shaped keys from tactic examples and user metadata while preserving local credential refs such as api_key_ref/apiKeyRef/apikeyref. Snake_case, kebab-case, camelCase, and collapsed lowercase secret keys such as api_key, x-api-key, apiKey, apikey, accessToken, accesstoken, clientSecret, and clientsecret are treated consistently. Cookie-style keys such as cookie, set-cookie, and sessionCookie are treated as secret-shaped metadata. SSE stream event metadata is filtered with the same public boundary before it is written to the response; event data remains the tactic output. Metadata maps must use string keys, including nested maps.

Error envelopes are stable across protocol and runtime failures.

{
  "detail": {
    "error": {
      "type": "SchemaError",
      "message": "Value does not match schema Question: ...",
      "tactic": "shout",
      "endpoint": "run",
      "request_id": "...",
      "metadata": {}
    }
  }
}

SchemaError and TacticUnsupportedError are 400 responses, an unknown name on a /tactics/{name}/... route is a 404 TacticNotFound, and anything else a tactic raises is a 500 (Services). The AAAX shell routes report errors in the same envelope.

docs.title: SSSN: the network module
docs.text:
SSSN, the Simple System of Systems Network, connects systems through channels. A channel is a named stream of records: producers append to it, consumers read it at their own pace, and every record can point back at the records it came from. A tactic is one system; channels are how its inputs arrive and its outputs leave. In code, SSSN is lllm.network.

SSSN is an experimental module of LLLM.

pip install "lllm-core[server,client]"   # adds the FastAPI store server and the HTTP clients

The data model, LocalStore, and TacticProcessor need only lllm-core.

docs.title: Five resources
docs.text:
Channel A named stream with a schema ref, a form, a description, and metadata. Event One append-only record in a channel: payload, kind, source, correlation id, and parent event ids. The store assigns its cursor. Subscription A named cursor over one channel, kept in the store so a consumer can stop and resume. Artifact Bytes stored by reference, with a media type and links to the events they belong to. Snapshot The latest value under a name, optionally pointing at the event that produced it.

All five are Pydantic models exported from lllm.network, and every store (LocalStore, RemoteStore, AsyncRemoteStore) reads and writes them with the same method names.

docs.title: A channel in ten lines
docs.text:
from lllm.network import Channel, Event, LocalStore

store = LocalStore(".lllm/network")
store.create_channel(Channel(name="inbox", description="Support messages."))

store.append_event(Event(channel="inbox", kind="message", payload={"text": "Checkout is down"}))
store.append_event(Event(channel="inbox", kind="message", payload={"text": "How do I export data?"}))

for event in store.query_events("inbox"):
    print(event.cursor, event.payload["text"])

1 Checkout is down
2 How do I export data?

LocalStore keeps a whole store in one folder: SQLite for channels, events, subscriptions, and snapshots, and plain files for artifact bytes. Serve that folder with lllm network serve and any process can use it through RemoteStore, which has the same methods.

docs.title: Tactics over channels
docs.text:
TacticProcessor joins the two halves of LLLM. It reads a channel through a named subscription, runs each event's payload through a tactic, and appends the output to a sink channel with a pointer back to the input. Continuing the example:

from lllm import as_tactic
from lllm.network import TacticProcessor


def triage(ticket: dict) -> dict:
    urgent = "down" in ticket["text"].lower().split()
    return {"priority": "urgent" if urgent else "normal"}


store.create_channel({"name": "triaged"})
processor = TacticProcessor(
    as_tactic(triage), store, source="inbox", sink="triaged", consumer="triage"
)

for result in processor.process():
    origin = store.get_event(result.parent_ids[0])
    print(result.payload, "<-", origin.payload["text"])

{'priority': 'urgent'} <- Checkout is down
{'priority': 'normal'} <- How do I export data?

Call processor.process() again and it returns []: the triage subscription lives in the store and remembers where it stopped, across restarts and across processes. Any tactic works here, including native tactics with agents and remote tactics (see The Tactic). Processing covers resuming, failures, async workers, and multi-stage pipelines.

docs.title: How the pieces fit
docs.text: flowchart LR P["Producer<br/>(app, script, curl)"] -->|append_event| IN["channel: inbox"] IN -->|subscription| TP["TacticProcessor<br/>runs a tactic"] TP -->|parent_ids, correlation_id| OUT["channel: triaged"] OUT -->|subscription| C["Consumers<br/>(dashboard, next stage)"] S[("LocalStore<br/>.lllm/network")] --- IN S --- OUT S --- API["create_app<br/>HTTP store API"] API --- R["RemoteStore /<br/>AsyncRemoteStore"] You want to Use Read Model channels, events, subscriptions, artifacts, snapshots Channel, Event, Subscription, Artifact, Snapshot Channels and stores Keep a store on disk LocalStore Channels and stores Run a tactic over a channel TacticProcessor Processing Serve a store over HTTP, add routes create_app, endpoint Serving Use a served store from another process RemoteStore, AsyncRemoteStore Serving Name channels with lllm:// refs ChannelRef, ChannelResolver, lllm.Resolver Serving Work from the shell lllm network --store DIR <command> Serving Mount channels next to tactics in one API lllm.shell AAAX

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
Names and wire formats may change between releases. Current limits worth knowing before you build on it:

  • One storage backend: LocalStore (SQLite plus files). The HTTP server and clients put any process in front of it.
  • Consumers poll. There is no push delivery or blocking pull.
  • pull_subscription moves the cursor as it returns events, so a consumer that pulls directly gets each event at most once. TacticProcessor acknowledges an event only after writing its output, so its delivery is at least once: an event cut short by a raised error or a crash runs again, and its output can appear twice. Processing shows how to keep failures visible.
  • The store server has no authentication. Bind it to localhost or put it behind your own gateway.

docs.text:

docs.title: Channels and stores
docs.text:
A store holds five kinds of resources: channels, events, subscriptions, artifacts, and snapshots. This page walks through each one with LocalStore. RemoteStore and AsyncRemoteStore expose the same methods over HTTP; see Serving for the few differences.

The examples run top to bottom as one session.

from lllm.network import LocalStore

store = LocalStore(".lllm/network")   # the folder is created if missing

LocalStore() with no argument uses .lllm/network relative to the working directory.

docs.title: Channels
docs.text:
A channel is a named stream. Create one from a Channel model or a plain dict:

from lllm.network import Channel

store.create_channel(
    Channel(
        name="inbox",
        schema="schemas.ticket",
        form="queue",
        description="Support messages as they arrive.",
        metadata={"owner": "support"},
    )
)
store.create_channel({"name": "triaged", "description": "One result per message."})

print([channel.name for channel in store.list_channels()])
print(store.get_channel("inbox").form)

['inbox', 'triaged']
queue
Field Meaning name Unique in the store. Must be a path segment: no whitespace, /, \, :, %, and not . or ... Letters, digits, -, _, and . are safe. schema Optional schema ref, such as a manifest key (schemas.ticket) or an import path. Recorded, not enforced. form How the channel is meant to be used. One of log (default), queue, topic, blackboard, latest-state, artifact-index, pipeline-edge, database-view, feed, time-series, tree, forum, hub. description Free text for people and tools. metadata Any JSON object.

The form is a declaration for readers and tools. LocalStore keeps every channel as an append-only log whatever its form. Channels cannot be updated or deleted through the API.

Creating a channel that already exists raises ChannelExistsError, so setup code that may run twice catches it:

from lllm.network import ChannelExistsError

try:
    store.create_channel({"name": "inbox"})
except ChannelExistsError as exc:
    print(exc)

Channel already exists: inbox

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
An event is one record in one channel. Events are append-only.

from lllm.network import Event

ticket = store.append_event(
    Event(
        channel="inbox",
        source="web-form",
        kind="message",
        payload={"text": "Checkout is down"},
        correlation_id="T-100",
        metadata={"locale": "en"},
    )
)
print(ticket.cursor, ticket.kind, ticket.correlation_id)

1 message T-100
Field Default Meaning id random UUID Unique in the store. You may set your own (a path segment); appending an id that exists raises EventExistsError. cursor assigned by the store Position in the store; see Cursors. channel required Must exist. timestamp now Seconds since the epoch, as a float. source None Who wrote it: a service, a processor, cli. kind "event" A token that consumers filter on (message, result, error, ...). payload None Any JSON value. Pydantic models are stored as JSON and read back as dicts. schema None Optional schema ref for the payload. metadata {} JSON object for small hints. correlation_id None Groups related events across channels: a ticket, a run, an episode. A token. parent_ids () Ids of the events this one was derived from, in any channel.

append_event returns the stored event with its cursor filled in. Pass a dict instead of an Event if you prefer; the same validation applies.

docs.title: Lineage
docs.text:
parent_ids and correlation_id make derived data traceable. The store rejects parent ids that do not exist, so every link resolves:

result = store.append_event(
    Event(
        channel="triaged",
        source="triage",
        kind="result",
        payload={"priority": "urgent"},
        correlation_id=ticket.correlation_id,
        parent_ids=(ticket.id,),
    )
)
print(store.get_event(result.parent_ids[0]).payload)

{'text': 'Checkout is down'}

TacticProcessor fills both fields for you; see Processing.

docs.title: Reading with cursors
docs.text:
query_events(channel, *, after_cursor=0, limit=100, kind=None) returns events with a cursor greater than after_cursor, oldest first:

store.append_event({"channel": "inbox", "kind": "message", "payload": {"text": "How do I export data?"}})
store.append_event({"channel": "inbox", "kind": "ping", "payload": {}})

print([(event.cursor, event.kind) for event in store.query_events("inbox")])
print([event.cursor for event in store.query_events("inbox", kind="message")])
print([event.cursor for event in store.query_events("inbox", after_cursor=ticket.cursor, limit=1)])

[(1, 'message'), (3, 'message'), (4, 'ping')]
[1, 3]
[3]

Cursor 2 is missing from inbox because it went to the event in triaged. Cursors increase across the whole store, so inside one channel they are ordered but have gaps. Never compute cursor + 1; resume from the last cursor you saw:

def read_all(store, channel, *, page=500):
    cursor = 0
    while batch := store.query_events(channel, after_cursor=cursor, limit=page):
        yield from batch
        cursor = batch[-1].cursor


print(sum(1 for _ in read_all(store, "inbox", page=2)))

3

after_cursor must be zero or more and limit at least 1; anything else raises InvalidPayloadError. get_event(event_id) reads one event by id.

docs.title: Subscriptions
docs.text:
A subscription is a cursor that the store keeps for a consumer, so the consumer can stop and pick up where it left off, from any process.

store.create_subscription(
    "inbox",
    subscription_id="dashboard",
    consumer="dashboard",
    batch_size=1,
    filters={"kind": "message"},
)

print([event.payload["text"] for event in store.pull_subscription("dashboard")])
print(store.get_subscription("dashboard").cursor)
print([event.payload["text"] for event in store.pull_subscription("dashboard", limit=10)])
print(store.pull_subscription("dashboard"))

['Checkout is down']
1
['How do I export data?']
()

How subscriptions behave:

  • pull_subscription(id, *, limit=None) returns up to limit (default: the subscription's batch_size) events after the stored cursor and moves the cursor past them in the same call. A pulled event is delivered once, whether or not the consumer finishes with it. TacticProcessor reads ahead with query_events instead and pulls an event only after writing its output; see Processing.
  • filters supports one key, kind. Other keys raise InvalidPayloadError.
  • Without subscription_id, the store generates a UUID. Name subscriptions you want to resume.
  • get_subscription(id) reads the current state without moving the cursor.

Creating a subscription with an id that already exists on the same channel returns the existing one unchanged, cursor and settings included. That makes create_subscription safe to call on every start:

same = store.create_subscription("inbox", subscription_id="dashboard", batch_size=50)
print(same.cursor, same.batch_size)

3 1

The cursor sits at 3, the last message event; the ping at cursor 4 never matched the filter. To change the filter or batch size, use a new id. Reusing an id on a different channel raises SubscriptionExistsError.

docs.title: Artifacts
docs.text:
Artifacts hold bytes that do not belong inline in an event: files, images, reports, model outputs.

artifact = store.write_artifact(
    b"%PDF-1.7 ...",
    channel="inbox",
    media_type="application/pdf",
    metadata={"filename": "march-invoice.pdf"},
    event_ids=(ticket.id,),
)
print(artifact.size, artifact.media_type, artifact.path == f"artifacts/{artifact.sha256}")
print(store.get_artifact(artifact.id).metadata)
print(store.read_artifact(artifact.id))

12 application/pdf True
{'filename': 'march-invoice.pdf'}
b'%PDF-1.7 ...'
  • write_artifact takes bytes, bytearray, or memoryview. channel and every id in event_ids must exist.
  • get_artifact returns the metadata (Artifact); read_artifact returns the bytes.
  • Files are content-addressed: the same bytes written twice produce two artifact records that share one file.

To let channel readers find an artifact, announce it with an event:

store.append_event(
    {
        "channel": "inbox",
        "kind": "attachment",
        "payload": {"artifact_id": artifact.id, "filename": "march-invoice.pdf"},
        "correlation_id": "T-100",
    }
)

docs.title: Snapshots
docs.text:
A snapshot is the latest value under a name: a queue depth, a current plan, the newest summary. Readers get it in one call instead of replaying a channel.

from lllm.network import Snapshot

store.put_snapshot(
    Snapshot(name="queue-depth", channel="inbox", value={"open": 2}, source_event_id=ticket.id)
)
print(store.get_snapshot("queue-depth").value)

store.put_snapshot({"name": "queue-depth", "value": {"open": 1}})
latest = store.get_snapshot("queue-depth")
print(latest.value, latest.channel, latest.source_event_id)

{'open': 2}
{'open': 1} None None

put_snapshot takes a Snapshot, a dict of snapshot fields, or a name and a value with the other fields as keywords, as in store.put_snapshot("queue-depth", {"open": 1}, channel="inbox"). The remote clients take the same arguments. It replaces the whole snapshot: fields you leave out are reset, as channel and source_event_id are above. channel and source_event_id must exist when set. Snapshots have no history; keep the history in a channel and point the snapshot at the event it came from.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Every store error is a subclass of NetworkError, itself a RuntimeError:

from lllm.network import NetworkError

for attempt in (
    lambda: store.get_channel("missing"),
    lambda: store.append_event({"channel": "inbox", "payload": {}, "parent_ids": ["nope"]}),
    lambda: store.append_event({"id": ticket.id, "channel": "inbox", "payload": {}}),
    lambda: store.query_events("inbox", after_cursor=-1),
    lambda: store.create_channel({"name": "bad name"}),
):
    try:
        attempt()
    except NetworkError as exc:
        print(type(exc).__name__)

ChannelNotFoundError
EventNotFoundError
EventExistsError
InvalidPayloadError
InvalidPayloadError
Error Raised when Store server status ChannelExistsError Creating a channel whose name is taken. 409 EventExistsError Appending an event whose id is taken. 409 SubscriptionExistsError Reusing a subscription id on a different channel. 409 ChannelNotFoundError Using a channel that does not exist. 404 EventNotFoundError Unknown event id, including dangling parent_ids, artifact event_ids, or snapshot source_event_id. 404 SubscriptionNotFoundError Unknown subscription id. 404 ArtifactNotFoundError Unknown artifact id, or its file is missing. 404 SnapshotNotFoundError Unknown snapshot name. 404 InvalidPayloadError Bad names, negative cursors, non-positive limits, unsupported filters, values that are not JSON serializable. 400 ChannelRefError Malformed or unbound lllm:// refs. Also a ValueError. not served

Over HTTP, RemoteStore raises RemoteStoreError with the status code and the error type name instead; see Serving.

docs.title: The LocalStore layout
docs.text:
.lllm/network/
  network.sqlite          # channels, events, subscriptions, artifact metadata, snapshots
  artifacts/
    cd98c5bce101ab55...   # artifact bytes, named by their SHA-256
  • An event's cursor is its SQLite rowid, which is why cursors are store-wide.
  • JSON values are stored with sorted keys, so payload dicts read back with their keys in alphabetical order.
  • Every call opens its own SQLite connection, so several processes can share a store folder, for example a store server and a local worker. SQLite serializes their writes.
  • Delete the folder to start over.

docs.title: Processing channels with tactics
docs.text:
TacticProcessor runs a tactic over the events of one channel. For each pending event it calls the tactic with the event's payload, which the tactic validates against its input type, and appends the output to a sink channel. Each output points back at its input through parent_ids and carries the input's correlation_id, so you can chain processors into pipelines and still trace every result to where it came from.

inbox ──subscription──▶ TacticProcessor(tactic) ──append──▶ triaged
Argument Default Meaning tactic required Any lllm Tactic: a subclass, as_tactic(fn), a native tactic with agents, a RemoteTactic. store required LocalStore or RemoteStore for process(); any store, including AsyncRemoteStore, for aprocess(). source required Channel to read. sink None Channel to append outputs to. Without one, outputs are returned instead. consumer "<tactic name>-<source>-processor", or "<tactic name>-<source>-<kind>-processor" with a kind Subscription id, and the source field of output events. See Resuming. kind None Only process source events of this kind. output_kind "result" kind of the output events. errors "raise" "raise" stops on the first failure and retries that event on the next call; "record" writes an error event and continues. See Failures.

The examples on this page run top to bottom as one session.

docs.title: One stage
docs.text:
import re

from pydantic import BaseModel

from lllm import Tactic
from lllm.network import Event, LocalStore, TacticProcessor

URGENT = re.compile(r"\b(down|outage|failing|broken)\b", re.IGNORECASE)


class Ticket(BaseModel):
    text: str


class Triage(BaseModel):
    priority: str
    summary: str


class TriageTicket(Tactic[Ticket, Triage]):
    name = "triage"
    input_type = Ticket
    output_type = Triage

    def _run(self, input_value, *, context=None):
        priority = "urgent" if URGENT.search(input_value.text) else "normal"
        return Triage(priority=priority, summary=input_value.text[:40])


store = LocalStore(".lllm/network")
store.create_channel({"name": "inbox"})
store.create_channel({"name": "triaged"})


def submit(text, ticket):
    store.append_event(
        Event(
            channel="inbox",
            source="web-form",
            kind="message",
            payload={"text": text},
            correlation_id=ticket,
        )
    )


submit("Checkout is down", "T-100")
submit("How do I export my data?", "T-101")

processor = TacticProcessor(TriageTicket(), store, source="inbox", sink="triaged")
for event in processor.process():
    print(event.source, event.kind, event.correlation_id, event.payload)

triage-inbox-processor result T-100 {'priority': 'urgent', 'summary': 'Checkout is down'}
triage-inbox-processor result T-101 {'priority': 'normal', 'summary': 'How do I export my data?'}

process() returns the sink events it wrote. Each one holds:

Field Value channel The sink. source The consumer name. kind output_kind ("result"). payload The tactic output as JSON. Pydantic models are dumped with model_dump(mode="json"). parent_ids (input_event.id,) correlation_id The input's correlation_id, or the input's id when it has none.

Create the sink channel before processing. The processor does not create channels.

docs.title: What the tactic sees
docs.text:
The tactic gets the event's payload as its input and a CallContext that describes the event:

Context field Value caller The consumer name. tags {"channel": <source>} metadata["event_id"] The input event's id. metadata["event_kind"] The input event's kind. metadata["correlation_id"] The input's correlation id, or its id. 
from lllm import as_tactic


def show_context(payload: dict, *, context=None) -> dict:
    return {
        "caller": context.caller,
        "tags": context.tags,
        "event_kind": context.metadata["event_kind"],
        "correlation_id": context.metadata["correlation_id"],
    }


peek = TacticProcessor(as_tactic(show_context), store, source="inbox", consumer="peek")
print(peek.process(limit=1))

[{'caller': 'peek', 'tags': {'channel': 'inbox'}, 'event_kind': 'message', 'correlation_id': 'T-100'}]

docs.title: Resuming
docs.text:
The consumer name is the id of a subscription that lives in the store. The first process() call creates it; every later processor with the same consumer, in this process or another one, continues from its cursor:

submit("Search is broken", "T-102")

restarted = TacticProcessor(TriageTicket(), store, source="inbox", sink="triaged")
print([event.correlation_id for event in restarted.process()])
print(store.get_subscription("triage-inbox-processor").cursor)

['T-102']
5

The default consumer joins the tactic's name (tactic.tactic_name, which is the function name for as_tactic(fn)), the source channel, and the kind filter if there is one: TriageTicket() reading inbox is triage-inbox-processor, and with kind="message" it would be triage-inbox-message-processor. Rules that follow from this:

  • Name consumers explicitly when two processors would share the default. The sink is not part of it, so a dry run without a sink and the real processor need different names (the dry run below uses consumer="dry-run").
  • If the default would contain whitespace, ?, or #, the constructor raises ValueError; pass consumer=.
  • To process a channel again from the start, use a new consumer name.
  • A subscription keeps the channel and kind filter it was created with. Reusing a consumer name with another channel or kind makes process() raise ValueError. With the default name, a new kind gives a new consumer, which starts at the beginning of the channel.
  • Run one worker per consumer name. Two workers sharing a consumer can process the same event twice, and with errors="raise" they can lose one.

docs.title: Failures
docs.text:
process() handles one event at a time. It reads the next event at the subscription cursor, runs the tactic, appends the output to the sink, and only then acknowledges the event, which moves the cursor past it. Delivery is therefore at least once: an event that was not acknowledged, because processing raised or the worker stopped, runs again on the next call. A tactic can see the same event twice, and the sink can then hold more than one output for it, so tactics should tolerate repeats. errors decides what a failure does.

With errors="raise" (the default), the exception propagates and the failing event stays pending. The next call runs it again, before any event behind it:

from lllm import SchemaError

store.append_event(
    Event(channel="inbox", kind="message", payload={"subject": "no text field"}, correlation_id="T-103")
)
submit("The API is down", "T-104")

for attempt in (1, 2):
    try:
        processor.process()
    except SchemaError as exc:
        print(f"attempt {attempt} failed:", type(exc).__name__)

attempt 1 failed: SchemaError
attempt 2 failed: SchemaError

T-103 fails input validation on every call, and T-104 waits behind it. With errors="record", a failure is written to the sink as a kind="error" event with the same lineage fields, the event is acknowledged, and processing continues. This processor reads the same triage-inbox-processor subscription, so it starts at T-103:

store.append_event(
    Event(channel="inbox", kind="message", payload={"subject": "still no text"}, correlation_id="T-105")
)

recording = TacticProcessor(
    TriageTicket(), store, source="inbox", sink="triaged", errors="record"
)
results = recording.process()
print([(event.kind, event.correlation_id) for event in results])
print(results[0].payload["type"])

[('error', 'T-103'), ('result', 'T-104'), ('error', 'T-105')]
SchemaError

The error payload is {"error": str(exc), "type": type(exc).__name__}. Use "record" in long-running workers, so one bad event cannot block the subscription and failures stay visible in the store; read them back with store.query_events("triaged", kind="error"). "record" needs a sink; without one, it acts like "raise".

Any exception counts as a failure: payloads that do not match the tactic's input type raise SchemaError, the tactic's own exceptions pass through unchanged, and so do errors from writing the output, such as the InvalidPayloadError for an output the store cannot encode as JSON. If the error event cannot be written either, as when the sink channel does not exist, process() raises and the event stays pending. Create channels up front.

docs.title: Without a sink
docs.text:
With no sink, process() returns the tactic outputs themselves. That is useful for dry runs, or when the results go somewhere other than a channel. limit caps how many results one call returns:

dry_run = TacticProcessor(TriageTicket(), store, source="inbox", consumer="dry-run")
print(dry_run.process(limit=2))

[Triage(priority='urgent', summary='Checkout is down'), Triage(priority='normal', summary='How do I export my data?')]

limit counts outputs and recorded errors alike. process() with no limit keeps going until the subscription has nothing pending.

docs.title: Remote and async stores
docs.text:
The processor only calls store methods, so a store served over HTTP works the same way. With lllm network serve --port 7700 running on this store:

from lllm.network import RemoteStore

remote = RemoteStore("http://127.0.0.1:7700")
remote.append_event(
    {"channel": "inbox", "kind": "message", "payload": {"text": "Exports time out"}, "correlation_id": "T-106"}
)

worker = TacticProcessor(TriageTicket(), remote, source="inbox", sink="triaged")
print([event.correlation_id for event in worker.process()])

['T-106']

The remote worker continued the triage-inbox-processor subscription where the local processors left it.

aprocess() is the async variant. It calls tactic.arun() and awaits store calls that return coroutines, so it works with AsyncRemoteStore as well as the sync stores. process() needs a sync store and raises TypeError when given an async one. This example talks to the store server in-process through httpx.ASGITransport, which is also how to test a worker without a running server; in production, pass only the URL.

import asyncio

import httpx

from lllm.network import AsyncRemoteStore, create_app


async def main():
    remote = AsyncRemoteStore(
        "http://store.local", transport=httpx.ASGITransport(app=create_app(store))
    )
    await remote.append_event(
        {"channel": "inbox", "kind": "message", "payload": {"text": "Uploads are failing"}, "correlation_id": "T-107"}
    )
    worker = TacticProcessor(TriageTicket(), remote, source="inbox", sink="triaged")
    return [event.correlation_id for event in await worker.aprocess()]


print(asyncio.run(main()))

['T-107']

docs.title: Pipelines
docs.text:
A pipeline is processors whose sink is the next one's source. Add a stage that drafts a reply for every triage result. The kind="result" filter skips the error events the first stage recorded:

class Reply(BaseModel):
    priority: str
    body: str


def draft_reply(result: Triage) -> Reply:
    opening = "We are on it." if result.priority == "urgent" else "Thanks for writing in."
    return Reply(priority=result.priority, body=f"{opening} Re: {result.summary}")


store.create_channel({"name": "replies"})

stages = [
    TacticProcessor(TriageTicket(), store, source="inbox", sink="triaged", errors="record"),
    TacticProcessor(
        as_tactic(draft_reply),
        store,
        source="triaged",
        sink="replies",
        consumer="draft-reply",
        kind="result",
    ),
]


def drain(processors):
    """Run every stage until none of them finds new events."""
    while any([processor.process() for processor in processors]):
        pass


submit("Refunds are failing for every customer", "T-108")
drain(stages)
print([(reply.correlation_id, reply.payload["priority"]) for reply in store.query_events("replies")])

[('T-100', 'urgent'), ('T-101', 'normal'), ('T-102', 'urgent'), ('T-104', 'urgent'), ('T-106', 'normal'), ('T-107', 'urgent'), ('T-108', 'urgent')]

The new ticket went through both stages in one drain; the earlier results reached the second stage because its draft-reply subscription started at the beginning of triaged.

docs.title: Tracing a result
docs.text:
parent_ids lead from any output back to the event that started the chain:

def lineage(store, event):
    """Follow parent_ids back to the event that started the chain."""
    chain = [event]
    while chain[-1].parent_ids:
        chain.append(store.get_event(chain[-1].parent_ids[0]))
    return chain


for event in lineage(store, store.query_events("replies")[-1]):
    print(f"{event.channel:8} {event.source:23} {event.payload}")

replies  draft-reply             {'body': 'We are on it. Re: Refunds are failing for every customer', 'priority': 'urgent'}
triaged  triage-inbox-processor  {'priority': 'urgent', 'summary': 'Refunds are failing for every customer'}
inbox    web-form                {'text': 'Refunds are failing for every customer'}

correlation_id groups the whole thread across channels without walking links:

print([
    (event.channel, event.kind)
    for channel in ("inbox", "triaged", "replies")
    for event in store.query_events(channel)
    if event.correlation_id == "T-108"
])

[('inbox', 'message'), ('triaged', 'result'), ('replies', 'result')]

docs.title: Fan-out
docs.text:
Each consumer has its own cursor, so several processors can read the same source and each sees every event:

def word_count(payload: dict) -> dict:
    return {"words": len(payload.get("text", "").split())}


store.create_channel({"name": "stats"})
stats = TacticProcessor(
    as_tactic(word_count), store, source="inbox", sink="stats", consumer="word-count"
)
print(len(stats.process()), "of", len(store.query_events("inbox")), "inbox events counted")

9 of 9 inbox events counted

docs.title: Latest state
docs.text:
To give readers the newest result without replaying a channel, write a snapshot that points at the event it came from:

latest = store.query_events("replies")[-1]
store.put_snapshot(
    {"name": "latest-reply", "channel": "replies", "value": latest.payload, "source_event_id": latest.id}
)
print(store.get_snapshot("latest-reply").value["body"])

We are on it. Re: Refunds are failing for every customer

docs.title: Running a worker
docs.text:
A worker is a loop around process() that sleeps when there is nothing to do:

import time


def run_worker(processor, *, idle_seconds=1.0):
    while True:
        if not processor.process(limit=100):
            time.sleep(idle_seconds)

The async version, for an AsyncRemoteStore or an event loop you already run:

import asyncio


async def run_async_worker(processor, *, idle_seconds=1.0):
    while True:
        if not await processor.aprocess(limit=100):
            await asyncio.sleep(idle_seconds)

Give each worker its own consumer name and errors="record", and stop it at any point: the next start resumes from the subscription cursor, and an event that was running when the worker stopped runs again. To serve the store these workers share, see Serving; to put workers, tactics, and channels behind one API, see AAAX.

docs.title: Serving stores
docs.text:
A store becomes a service with one call: create_app(store) returns a FastAPI app that exposes every store operation over HTTP. RemoteStore and AsyncRemoteStore call that API with the same methods as LocalStore, so code written against a local store runs against a remote one by swapping the constructor (the few differences are listed under Clients). Refs (lllm://org/package/channels/name) let code name a channel and leave the choice of store to a config file.

pip install "lllm-core[server,client]"

docs.title: Serve a store
docs.text:
From the shell:

lllm network --store .lllm/network serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 7700

--store defaults to .lllm/network and --port to 7700. In Python, the app is a regular ASGI app:

import uvicorn

from lllm.network import LocalStore, create_app

app = create_app(LocalStore(".lllm/network"))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run(app, host="127.0.0.1", port=7700)

create_app() without a store opens LocalStore(".lllm/network") in the working directory. The app keeps the store at app.state.network_store.

The server has no authentication. Keep it on localhost or put it behind a gateway that handles access control.

docs.title: HTTP API
docs.text:
Method and path Body or query Returns GET /health {"ok": true} POST /channels a channel: name, schema, form, description, metadata the channel GET /channels all channels GET /channels/{name} one channel POST /events an event: channel, payload, kind, source, schema, metadata, correlation_id, parent_ids, optional id and timestamp the stored event, with cursor GET /events ?channel=...&after_cursor=0&limit=100&kind=... events, oldest first GET /events/{id} one event POST /subscriptions channel, id, consumer, batch_size, filters, metadata the subscription (existing one if the id is taken on the same channel) GET /subscriptions/{id} the subscription and its cursor POST /subscriptions/{id}/pull ?limit=... pending events; moves the cursor POST /artifacts data, encoding (text or base64), channel, media_type, metadata, event_ids artifact metadata GET /artifacts/{id} the raw bytes, with the artifact's media type GET /artifacts/{id}/metadata artifact metadata PUT /snapshots/{name} value, channel, timestamp, schema, source_event_id, metadata the snapshot (replaces any previous value) GET /snapshots/{name} the snapshot

FastAPI also serves the OpenAPI schema at /openapi.json and interactive docs at /docs.

curl -s -w '\n' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7700/channels \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"name": "inbox"}'
curl -s -w '\n' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7700/events \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"channel": "inbox", "kind": "message", "payload": {"text": "Checkout is down"}}'
curl -s -w '\n' "http://127.0.0.1:7700/events?channel=inbox&limit=10"

{"name":"inbox","schema":null,"form":"log","description":"","metadata":{}}
{"id":"6857626f-ce8f-4240-adee-0ac098a3622e","cursor":1,"channel":"inbox","timestamp":1793846751.1789103,"source":null,"kind":"message","payload":{"text":"Checkout is down"},"schema":null,"metadata":{},"correlation_id":null,"parent_ids":[]}
[{"id":"6857626f-ce8f-4240-adee-0ac098a3622e","cursor":1,"channel":"inbox","timestamp":1793846751.1789103,"source":null,"kind":"message","payload":{"text":"Checkout is down"},"schema":null,"metadata":{},"correlation_id":null,"parent_ids":[]}]

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Errors come back in one envelope, with the error class name as type:

curl -s -w '\n' http://127.0.0.1:7700/channels/missing

{"detail":{"error":{"type":"ChannelNotFoundError","message":"Channel not found: missing"}}}
Status When 400 InvalidPayloadError, other NetworkErrors, and request bodies that fail validation (reported as InvalidPayloadError). 404 ChannelNotFoundError, EventNotFoundError, SubscriptionNotFoundError, ArtifactNotFoundError, SnapshotNotFoundError. 409 ChannelExistsError, EventExistsError (an event id that is taken), SubscriptionExistsError. 500 Anything else, with the exception's class name and message.

docs.title: Custom endpoints
docs.text:
Add domain routes next to the built-in ones with the endpoint decorators (endpoint.get, .post, .put, .patch, .delete) and pass the functions to create_app:

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from lllm.network import InvalidPayloadError, LocalStore, create_app, endpoint


@endpoint.get("/channels/{name}/count", scope="channel", tags=("stats",))
def count_events(store, name: str, params=None):
    """Count the events in a channel, or only those of one ?kind=."""
    kind = (params or {}).get("kind")
    total, cursor = 0, 0
    while batch := store.query_events(name, after_cursor=cursor, limit=500, kind=kind):
        total += len(batch)
        cursor = batch[-1].cursor
    return {"channel": name, "kind": kind, "events": total}


@endpoint.post("/channels/{name}/messages", scope="channel")
def post_message(store, name: str, body=None):
    """Append a message event from a {"text": ...} body."""
    if not isinstance(body, dict) or not isinstance(body.get("text"), str):
        raise InvalidPayloadError('body must be {"text": "..."}')
    event = store.append_event(
        {"channel": name, "kind": "message", "source": "api", "payload": {"text": body["text"]}}
    )
    return {"id": event.id, "cursor": event.cursor}


store = LocalStore(".lllm/network")
store.create_channel({"name": "inbox"})
app = create_app(store, custom_endpoints=[count_events, post_message])

client = TestClient(app)
client.post("/channels/inbox/messages", json={"text": "Checkout is down"})
print(client.get("/channels/inbox/count").json())
print(client.get("/channels/inbox/count", params={"kind": "ping"}).json())
print(client.post("/channels/inbox/messages", json={"txt": "typo"}).json())

{'channel': 'inbox', 'kind': None, 'events': 1}
{'channel': 'inbox', 'kind': 'ping', 'events': 0}
{'detail': {'error': {'type': 'InvalidPayloadError', 'message': 'body must be {"text": "..."}'}}}

How arguments are bound:

  • A parameter named store receives the store.
  • A parameter named body receives the parsed JSON body (None for GET, DELETE, or a body that is not JSON).
  • Any other parameter is filled from a path parameter of the same name.
  • A parameter named params that is not a path parameter receives the query string as a dict of strings; for a repeated key, the last value wins.
  • Anything else keeps its default. A parameter without one fails every request with a 500 TypeError.

The function may return any JSON-encodable value, or be async. Exceptions map to statuses like the built-in routes, so raise NetworkError subclasses for 4xx responses.

Routes must not collide with the built-in ones (GET /channels/{x} is taken, whatever the parameter is called), and endpoint names and method-plus-path pairs must be unique; create_app raises ValueError otherwise. Functions without a decorator are ignored. The decorator arguments are metadata: name (defaults to the function name), scope (store, channel, subscription, artifact, or snapshot), description (defaults to the docstring), and tags show up in the OpenAPI schema and in channel_resource.

docs.title: Clients
docs.text:
RemoteStore is the synchronous client, AsyncRemoteStore the async one. Both take base_url, timeout=30.0, and an optional httpx transport, and both have the LocalStore methods. With the store from the previous sections served on port 7700:

from lllm.network import RemoteStore, RemoteStoreError

store = RemoteStore("http://127.0.0.1:7700")
event = store.append_event(
    {"channel": "inbox", "kind": "message", "payload": {"text": "Search is broken"}}
)
print(event.cursor, store.get_event(event.id).payload)

store.put_snapshot("queue-depth", {"open": 2}, channel="inbox", source_event_id=event.id)
print(store.get_snapshot("queue-depth").value)

try:
    store.get_channel("missing")
except RemoteStoreError as exc:
    print(exc.status_code, exc.error_type, exc.message)

2 {'text': 'Search is broken'}
{'open': 2}
404 ChannelNotFoundError Channel not found: missing

Where the clients differ from LocalStore:

Method LocalStore RemoteStore / AsyncRemoteStore write_artifact bytes, bytearray, or memoryview bytes (sent base64-encoded) or str (sent as UTF-8 text) errors NetworkError subclasses RemoteStoreError for server errors, with status_code, error_type, message, and the raw detail. Names and ids are checked before sending and raise InvalidPayloadError.

RemoteStoreError is a RuntimeError, not a NetworkError; branch on error_type (for example "SubscriptionNotFoundError") or status_code. Each call opens its own short-lived HTTP connection.

put_snapshot has the same signature on every store: put_snapshot(snapshot=None, value=None, *, name=None, channel=None, timestamp=None, schema=None, source_event_id=None, metadata=None). Pass a Snapshot or a dict of snapshot fields, or a name and a value. The value is stored exactly as given, so put_snapshot("config", {"value": 3, "unit": "ms"}) stores the whole dict. The one exception is a Snapshot passed as the value: its fields are stored under the name.

AsyncRemoteStore has the same methods as coroutines. Pass httpx.ASGITransport to call an app in-process, which is the easiest way to test code that uses a remote store:

import asyncio

import httpx

from lllm.network import AsyncRemoteStore, LocalStore, create_app


async def main():
    app = create_app(LocalStore("test-store"))
    store = AsyncRemoteStore("http://test", transport=httpx.ASGITransport(app=app))
    await store.create_channel({"name": "inbox"})
    await store.append_event({"channel": "inbox", "payload": {"text": "hi"}})
    return [event.payload for event in await store.query_events("inbox")]


print(asyncio.run(main()))

[{'text': 'hi'}]

docs.title: Refs and .lllm/config.toml
docs.text:
A channel ref names a channel by package, not by location:

lllm://<org>/<package>/channels/<name>
lllm://<org>/<package>/snapshots/<name>

ChannelRef parses and validates one:

from lllm.network import ChannelRef

ref = ChannelRef("lllm://demo/support-desk/channels/inbox")
print(ref.org, ref.package, ref.resource_kind, ref.name)

demo support-desk channels inbox

A project binds refs to stores in .lllm/config.toml, the same file that binds tactic refs (see Refs). Each binding has exactly one target:

[refs."lllm://demo/support-desk/channels/inbox"]
store = ".lllm/network"            # a LocalStore folder, relative to the project root

[refs."lllm://demo/support-desk/channels/triaged"]
url = "http://127.0.0.1:7700"      # a served store
owner = "support"                  # extra keys are kept as binding metadata

[refs."lllm://demo/support-desk/snapshots/latest-reply"]
store = "archive"                  # names the [stores.archive] table below

[stores.archive]
path = "data/support-store"        # relative to the project root

ChannelResolver reads the /channels/ and /snapshots/ bindings and ignores the others (tactics, services, schemas, ...), which other resolvers read from the same file:

from lllm.network import ChannelResolver

channels = ChannelResolver.from_config(".")
print(channels.refs())

triaged = channels.resolve("lllm://demo/support-desk/channels/triaged")
print(triaged.name, triaged.url, triaged.metadata)

print(type(channels.local_store("lllm://demo/support-desk/channels/inbox")).__name__)
print(type(channels.client("lllm://demo/support-desk/channels/triaged")).__name__)
print(channels.store_path("lllm://demo/support-desk/snapshots/latest-reply").relative_to(channels.root))

('lllm://demo/support-desk/channels/inbox', 'lllm://demo/support-desk/channels/triaged', 'lllm://demo/support-desk/snapshots/latest-reply')
triaged http://127.0.0.1:7700 {'owner': 'support'}
LocalStore
RemoteStore
data/support-store
Method Returns ChannelResolver.from_config(path) A resolver for path/.lllm/config.toml, or for a config file path. Relative store paths resolve against the folder that contains .lllm/. The file must exist. ChannelResolver.from_text(text, *, root=None) A resolver for config text, parsed in memory. Relative store paths resolve against root (default: the working directory). Writes no files. ChannelResolver(root=".") and bind(ref, *, url=None, store=None, path=None, metadata=None) Bind refs in code. resolve(ref) A ResolvedChannelRef: ref, resource_kind, name, url, store, path, metadata. local_store(ref), store_path(ref) A LocalStore (or its path) for store/path bindings. client(ref), async_client(ref) A RemoteStore or AsyncRemoteStore for url bindings; both accept timeout= and transport=. refs() The bound refs, sorted.

Malformed refs and unbound refs raise ChannelRefError. path is always a folder path. store is one too, unless it names a [stores.<name>] table: then the binding uses that table's path (ChannelRefError if the table has none). channels.stores() returns the tables.

A ref resolves to a whole store; the channel inside it is the ref's last segment. To get a store for any ref without caring which kind of binding it has, use lllm.Resolver, which reads tactic, channel, and snapshot bindings from the same file:

from lllm import Resolver

resolver = Resolver.from_config(".")
ref = "lllm://demo/support-desk/channels/triaged"

store = resolver.store(ref)            # LocalStore or RemoteStore, per the binding
print(type(store).__name__, ChannelRef(ref).name)
print(type(resolver.resolve("lllm://demo/support-desk/channels/inbox")).__name__)

RemoteStore triaged
LocalStore

resolver.resolve(ref) returns a tactic for /tactics/ refs and a store for /channels/ and /snapshots/ refs. Tutorial 11 uses it to point a worker at a served store.

docs.title: Package metadata
docs.text:
A package declares its channels and snapshots in lllm.toml (see The manifest):

[channels.inbox]
form = "log"
description = "Support messages as they arrive."

[channels.triaged]
form = "log"
description = "One triage result per message."

[snapshots.latest-reply]
channel = "triaged"
description = "The newest drafted reply."

A channel's form must be one of the forms listed in Channels and stores; load_manifest rejects any other value.

open_package_store(manifest, *, store=None) opens the package's store, <package>/.lllm/network by default, and creates every declared channel that does not exist yet. For a package folder support-desk/ whose lllm.toml has a [package] table and the sections above:

from lllm.hub import load_manifest
from lllm.network.resources import open_package_store

manifest = load_manifest("support-desk")
store = open_package_store(manifest)
print(store.root.relative_to(manifest.base_dir), [channel.name for channel in store.list_channels()])

.lllm/network ['inbox', 'triaged']

lllm serve uses it to serve a package's channels as a store:

lllm serve support-desk --resource channels.inbox --port 7700

That serves the whole package store (every declared channel), not only inbox; --store DIR picks another folder.

channel_resource and snapshot_resource go the other way: they turn models into the dictionaries the hub indexes, including custom endpoint metadata:

import json

from lllm.network import Channel, Snapshot, channel_resource, snapshot_resource

print(json.dumps(channel_resource(
    Channel(name="inbox", form="log", description="Support messages as they arrive."),
    custom_endpoints=[count_events],
), indent=2))
print(snapshot_resource(Snapshot(name="latest-reply", channel="triaged"), description="The newest drafted reply."))

lllm network works on a local store folder. --store DIR (default .lllm/network) goes before the command, as in lllm network --store ../other/.lllm/network channels; the folder is created if it does not exist. lllm network create-channel inbox --description "Support messages."

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text:
A guided path from a one-line chat to served, packaged, connected agentic systems. Lessons 1 to 8 teach the native runtime; 9 to 11 take a system outward.

# Lesson What you will learn 1 Quick Start Tactic.quick(), open → receive → respond, local models, lllm create 2 Agents and Dialogs The core mental model: Agent, Dialog, multi-turn chats, forking 3 Prompts and Structured Output Templates, parsers, Pydantic output, exception handlers, prompt inheritance 4 Tools, Proxies, and Sandbox @tool, the tool loop, MCP, proxies with run_python and CALL_API 5 Native Tactics Multi-agent programs, call sessions, sub-tactics, batch and async 6 Packages and the Hub lllm.toml, discovery, YAML agent configs, validating and publishing 7 Logging and Cost Tracking Loggers, call sessions and cost, observers 8 Advanced Patterns Proxy orchestration, forking, pipelines, streaming, offline testing 9 Serving and Composition lllm serve, the HTTP API, remote tactics, refs, lllm.Resolver 10 Pydantic AI Agents Pydantic AI agents as tactics, tactics as Pydantic AI tools 11 Channels with SSSN Channels, TacticProcessor, serving a store, AAAX strategies

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.10+
  • pip install "lllm-core[native,server]"
